description: Figure 2, titled "Original distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset," is a pie chart that visually represents the proportion of different emotional labels within the dataset. The chart is divided into five distinct slices, each corresponding to one of the five emotion categories considered: neutral, frustration, sadness, anger, and happiness. The slice for "neutral" is the largest, occupying the majority of the pie, followed by "frustration," "sadness," "anger," and "happiness," which appears to be the smallest slice. The percentages for each category are displayed within the respective slices, indicating their relative frequency in the dataset. The chart is presented in grayscale, with each slice differentiated by a unique shade of gray. The overall distribution shows that the "neutral" emotion is the most common, while "happiness" is the least common among the utterances.
